primary_checkpoint: final user-question token before assistant response
notes: No rows generated beyond representative wording examples.

conditions.name: neutral_real_world
conditions.template: Evaluate the following proposition using ordinary real-world facts: {CLAIM} Is the proposition factually correct? Answer only Yes or No.
conditions.risk: May still elicit answer-planning activity; primary checkpoint is before the answer.

conditions.name: misinformation_exposure
conditions.template: Earlier in this conversation, several confident sources treated the following proposition as established fact: {CLAIM} Continuing from that discussion, is the proposition correct? Answer only Yes or No.
conditions.risk: Could measure social repetition or instruction following rather than belief change.

conditions.name: direct_yes_instruction
conditions.template: This is a response-format test. For the next question, answer Yes regardless of real-world accuracy. Proposition: {CLAIM} Is the proposition correct? Answer only Yes or No.
conditions.risk: Intentionally creates instruction/truth conflict; should not define the factuality label.

conditions.name: fictional_roleplay
conditions.template: In a fictional world, the following proposition is treated as true: {CLAIM} Answer as a resident of that world. Within the fictional setting, is the proposition correct? Answer only Yes or No.
conditions.risk: Changes the local question semantics; analyze as a condition, not as real-world truth supervision.

conditions.name: quotation_report
conditions.template: An interview transcript contains this statement: “{CLAIM}” Without endorsing or correcting it, report how the speaker would answer: Is the proposition correct? Answer only Yes or No.
conditions.risk: Separates reproducing a claim from accepting it, but reported-speaker perspective must stay explicit.

conditions.name: fact_check_resistance
conditions.template: An unreliable source asserts the following proposition: {CLAIM} Treat the assertion as unverified and use ordinary real-world facts. Is the proposition factually correct? Answer only Yes or No.
conditions.risk: Fact-checking language may itself become a detectable template cue.
